content_html:
See the cost, tokens, tool calls and traces of Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Qwen Code on your own machine, with one docker compose up.

한국어 · 简体中文

agent-otel-kit is a local OpenTelemetry stack for AI coding agents: an OpenTelemetry Collector that receives the agents' OTLP telemetry, Prometheus for metrics, Loki for events, Tempo for traces, and the same three dashboards in Grafana and in Perses. A small Go CLI points each agent at the collector and checks that data arrives.

Quickstart (30 seconds)

Requirements: Docker with the compose plugin, and the CLI (see Install the CLI).

git clone https://github.com/s3onghyun/agent-otel-kit && cd agent-otel-kit
docker compose up -d                       # or: make up
brew install s3onghyun/tap/agent-otel-kit  # or a release archive, go install, or make build
agent-otel-kit setup claude                # or codex, gemini, qwen, all
# start a new agent session and use it for a minute, then:
agent-otel-kit doctor

Open Grafana at http://localhost:3000 (anonymous read access; the dashboards are in the "Agent OTel Kit" folder). For Perses, run docker compose --profile perses up -d and open http://localhost:8080.

Every port is bound to 127.0.0.1. The collector listens on localhost:4318 (OTLP/HTTP) and localhost:4317 (OTLP/gRPC).

Install the CLI

  • Homebrew (macOS, Linux): brew install s3onghyun/tap/agent-otel-kit
  • Prebuilt archives for Linux and macOS (amd64, arm64) with checksums.txt: Releases
  • Go 1.24+: go install github.com/s3onghyun/agent-otel-kit/cmd/agent-otel-kit@latest
  • From the clone: make build writes bin/agent-otel-kit

agent-otel-kit version prints the version, commit and build date.

What is collected and what is not

Collected: the metrics, events and traces each agent exports when telemetry is on: cost (Claude Code only), token counts by type, sessions, active time, tool calls with name, success, duration and permission decision, model request duration, and trace spans for each prompt, model request and tool call.

Not collected by default:

  • Prompt text, model responses, tool arguments, tool output, file paths, shell commands and error messages (including error.message and span exception messages, which can hold file paths). The agents already redact most of these unless you opt in (OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS, OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS, Codex log_user_prompt, Gemini and Qwen Code logPrompts). The collector deletes these attributes again in transform/redact, so turning one of those agent switches on by mistake does not store content. Set AGENT_OTEL_KIT_CAPTURE_CONTENT=true in the collector's environment to keep them.
  • The process command line (process.command_args). Gemini CLI sends it as a resource attribute, and for gemini -p "..." it contains the prompt.
  • user.email. Claude Code attaches the account email to every data point, and Gemini CLI documents the same for Google sign-in (with an API key it sent none); the collector drops it unless AGENT_OTEL_KIT_KEEP_EMAIL=true.
  • setup gemini and setup qwen set logPrompts: false, because Gemini CLI and Qwen Code log prompts by default. Qwen Code also sends the final answer of its background subagents (result, execution_summary) with prompt logging off; the collector deletes those too.

Other identifiers stay: session.id (Codex: conversation.id), user.account_uuid, organization.id, Codex user.account_id, installation.id, terminal.type, host name and OS. Everything stays on your machine; nothing in the stack sends data elsewhere (Grafana and Loki usage reporting is off).

Per-agent setup

setup edits only the agent's own user config file. The first run saves the original file under ~/.agent-otel-kit/backups/; setup --undo <agent> puts back the exact original bytes and permissions, or deletes the file (and any directory) that setup created. If you edited the file after setup, undo refuses unless you pass --force. --dry-run prints the result without writing. --endpoint points agents at a collector elsewhere (default http://localhost:4318).

Agent File What setup writes
Claude Code ~/.claude/settings.json ($CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR honoured) env: CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1, OTLP exporters for metrics and logs, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, http/protobuf, a 10 s metric interval, and the traces beta (OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp, CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1; skip with --no-traces)
Codex ~/.codex/config.toml ($CODEX_HOME honoured) a marked block under [otel]: exporter, trace_exporter and metrics_exporter as otlp-http with the /v1/logs, /v1/traces, /v1/metrics URLs, log_user_prompt = false; other [otel] keys and the rest of the file are kept
Gemini CLI ~/.gemini/settings.json telemetry: enabled, target: "local", otlpEndpoint, otlpProtocol: "http", logPrompts: false; removes outfile, which would override the endpoint
Qwen Code ~/.qwen/settings.json telemetry: enabled, target: "local", otlpEndpoint, otlpProtocol, logPrompts: false; removes outfile and the per-signal otlpTracesEndpoint, otlpLogsEndpoint, otlpMetricsEndpoint, which would override the endpoint. A file setup creates also gets "$version": 4, so Qwen Code does not rewrite it on first start. privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled (Qwen Code's own usage statistics) is left as it is

Settings files with comments are not edited (setup stops with an error); add the block by hand in that case.

Qwen Code uses OTLP/gRPC by default (otlpProtocol: "grpc", otlpEndpoint: "http://localhost:4317"), because its OTLP/HTTP exporter has an open report of sending empty request bodies (QwenLM/qwen-code#14466); OTLP/HTTP worked in the 0.27.4 runs below. setup takes the gRPC endpoint from --endpoint by replacing port 4318 with 4317. When --endpoint is on another port (for example setup all --endpoint https://otel.lan/otlp), setup writes the --endpoint URL with otlpProtocol: "http" instead and prints a notice. --protocol http always writes OTLP/HTTP; --protocol grpc always writes gRPC and fails for an endpoint not on port 4318.

Supported versions:

Agent Status
Claude Code 2.1.325 Verified on a live stack: metrics, events and traces (with the traces beta flag).
Codex 0.169.0 (codex exec) Verified on a live stack with setup codex: metrics, events and traces. Tokens come from the codex.turn.token_usage histogram, sessions from codex.thread.started, tool calls from codex.tool_result events. No cost metric. Codex metrics carry no session ID, so Codex sessions are missing from the per-session table.
Gemini CLI 0.68.0 (gemini -p, API key) Verified on a live stack with setup gemini: metrics, events and traces. Tool calls come from gemini_cli.tool_call events. No cost metric.
Qwen Code 0.27.4 (qwen -p, OpenAI-compatible auth) Verified on a live stack with setup qwen (gRPC) and setup qwen --protocol http: metrics, events and traces, with a read_file call and a denied shell call. Tool calls come from qwen-code.tool_call events. No cost metric. The model server was a local OpenAI-compatible mock with a dummy key, not a real provider.

Only the non-interactive modes and the auth methods listed were run. Gemini CLI with a personal Google login was rejected by Google for this client ("no longer supported for Gemini Code Assist for individuals"), so that path was tested with an AI Studio API key. Qwen Code was run against a mock OpenAI-compatible server: the telemetry path is the same with a real Alibaba Cloud Model Studio (DashScope) or DeepSeek key, but such a run would additionally show the model names, token counts (cache and reasoning tokens) and latencies those providers really report.

The delta temporality trap

Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI export counters with delta temporality by default (each export carries only the increase since the last one; Qwen Code sends cumulative counters), and Prometheus only stores cumulative counters, so a plain OTLP-to-Prometheus path drops or misreads them. The collector's delta_to_cumulative processor keeps a running total per series before the Prometheus exporter, so the agents can keep their defaults.

Two related Prometheus settings in compose.yaml: created-timestamp-zero-ingestion inserts a zero sample when a series starts, so a short session's first export is counted, and promql-extended-range-selectors enables increase(x[$__range] anchored), which the dashboards use for exact totals without increase()'s extrapolation.

Dashboards

All three exist in Grafana (grafana/dashboards/) and Perses (perses/provisioning/dashboards/). Both are generated from one panel list in tools/gendashboards (make dashboards); CI fails if the committed JSON differs.

Agent cost and tokens: cost, estimated cost (see third-party endpoints), tokens, sessions and active time for the range; cost per interval by model; tokens per interval by type; cost by model; tokens by agent, model and type; the most expensive sessions. The Cost basis selector filters cost by cost_basis.

Agent tool calls: call count, failures, success rate and p95 duration; calls per interval and p95 duration by tool; a per-tool table; permission decisions (who allowed each call); failed calls from Loki. The tool metric agent_otel_kit.tool.duration is built in the collector by the signal_to_metrics connector from each agent's tool result events, so it is the same for all agents.

Agent sessions and traces: per-session cost and tokens, the interaction traces from Tempo, a trace waterfall (paste a trace ID into the Trace ID box), model request duration, event rate by type, and the event stream of the selected sessions.

Every label is normalized to agent_name (claude-code, codex, gemini-cli, qwen-code), derived from the service.name each agent sets. Set OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=agent.name=<name> on an agent to override it. Claude Code's own agent.name attribute (the subagent name) and Codex's agent_name attribute (the agent path, /root for the main agent) are kept as subagent.name. Codex's conversation.id is copied to session.id, and its token_type to type.

Token totals (the Tokens stat and the per-session Tokens column) add only token types that do not overlap: Codex counts cached input inside input and reasoning inside output, Gemini CLI counts cache inside input, and Qwen Code counts cache inside input and, with OpenAI-compatible providers, thought (reasoning) inside output, so those parts (and Codex's total) are not added again. Claude Code's cacheRead and cacheCreation are separate from input and are added. The per-type breakdowns show every type, including the overlapping ones.

Agent differences visible on the dashboards:

  • Codex marks a shell command that ran but exited non-zero as a successful tool call. In code mode it also reports the outer exec tool next to each inner exec_command.
  • Codex sends many short internal traces (auth, fs.read_file, ...); the traces panel lists only turn/start for Codex. Gemini CLI has no per-prompt trace: it sends one llm_call trace per model call and one schedule_tool_calls trace per tool batch.
  • Over its default WebSocket transport, Codex logs no per-request model duration, so the model request panel shows Codex only for HTTP /responses requests.
  • Qwen Code sends one qwen-code.interaction trace per prompt. Model calls of its background subagents (such as the memory extractor) arrive as separate qwen-code.llm_request traces, which the traces panel does not list.
  • Qwen Code adds session.id to metrics only with "telemetry": {"metrics": {"includeSessionId": true}} in ~/.qwen/settings.json (or QWEN_TELEMETRY_METRICS_INCLUDE_SESSION_ID=true). setup leaves it off, because Qwen Code warns that it creates new time series for every session, so without it Qwen Code sessions are missing from the per-session table. Events and spans always carry session.id.

Metric names seen in Prometheus from Claude Code 2.1.325: claude_code_cost_usage_USD_total, claude_code_token_usage_tokens_total, claude_code_session_count_total, claude_code_active_time_seconds_total. From Codex 0.169.0 (74 metric families in a short codex exec run), among them: codex_turn_token_usage_{bucket,count,sum} (label token_type), codex_thread_started_total, codex_tool_call_total, codex_turn_e2e_duration_ms_milliseconds_*. From Gemini CLI 0.68.0: gemini_cli_token_usage_total (label type: input, output, thought, cache, tool), gemini_cli_session_count_total, gemini_cli_tool_call_count_total, gemini_cli_api_request_count_total. From Qwen Code 0.27.4: qwen_code_token_usage_total (label type: input, output, thought, cache), qwen_code_session_count_total, qwen_code_tool_call_count_total (labels function_name, decision, success), qwen_code_api_request_count_total, qwen_code_api_request_latency_milliseconds_*. From the collector: agent_otel_kit_tool_duration_milliseconds_{bucket,count,sum}.

Event names seen in Loki: Claude Code tool_result, tool_decision, api_request, user_prompt, ...; Codex codex.tool_result, codex.tool_decision, codex.sse_event, codex.api_request, codex.user_prompt, ...; Gemini CLI gemini_cli.tool_call, gemini_cli.api_request, gemini_cli.api_response, gemini_cli.file_operation, gemini_cli.user_prompt, ...; Qwen Code qwen-code.tool_call, qwen-code.api_request, qwen-code.api_response, qwen-code.file_operation, qwen-code.user_prompt, .... Claude Code also defines claude_code.lines_of_code.count, claude_code.commit.count, claude_code.pull_request.count and claude_code.code_edit_tool.decision, which only appear after edits, commits or pull requests.

The screenshots were taken from this stack with real sessions run on the author's machine: Claude Code (make demo), codex exec, gemini -p and Qwen Code 0.27.4 (qwen -p, against a local OpenAI-compatible mock model server with a dummy key), then make screenshots. The demo GIF at the top is a headless Chromium recording of the same dashboards during one such run, only trimmed and sped up; docs/demo.mp4 is its source.

Claude Code with third-party (Anthropic-compatible) endpoints

DeepSeek, Z.ai (GLM), Moonshot (Kimi), MiniMax and Alibaba Model Studio publish guides for running Claude Code against their Anthropic-compatible APIs through ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. Claude Code then exports the same telemetry as usual, and the kit receives it without changes. What the dashboards show, measured with Claude Code 2.1.325 against a local mock of such an endpoint (not yet against the providers themselves):

  • Token counts are exact: they are the usage numbers the endpoint returns.
  • Cost is not. Claude Code computes cost locally at Anthropic rates. A model ID it does not know (deepseek-chat, glm-4.6) is priced at the rate of its default model ($4 input, $20 output, $0.20 cache read per million tokens in 2.1.325). When the provider maps Claude model IDs on its side (Claude Code sends claude-opus-5-5, the provider runs its own model), the metrics say claude-opus-5-5 at Claude list price. The model that answered appears only in the api_request event's model, and only if the provider returns its real name.
  • Every metric, event and span of such a session carries anthropic.custom_base_url=true (Prometheus label anthropic_custom_base_url). The kit keeps it.

What the collector does with it:

  • It labels each Claude Code cost series and api_request event with cost_basis: estimated when anthropic.custom_base_url is true, otherwise list. A cost.basis you set on the agent yourself is kept (see below). The cost dashboard shows Cost (USD) (list and managed) and Estimated cost (USD) as separate numbers, and names the basis in every cost series and in the session tables.
  • It strips a context-window suffix such as [1m] from model on Claude Code metrics, events and spans. The provider guides write model IDs as deepseek-flash[1m]; Claude Code sends deepseek-flash to the API but keeps the suffix in its telemetry, which would split one model into two series. Claude Code's own [1m] model IDs are merged the same way.

Exact cost: modelPricing in managed settings

Claude Code (v2.1.242 or later) prices models from a modelPricing.overrides table, and applies it to the OpenTelemetry cost metric and events too. It reads the table only from managed settings, which need root or administrator rights:

  • Linux: /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json
  • macOS: /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-settings.json
{
  "modelPricing": {
    "overrides": {
      "deepseek-flash": { "input": INPUT, "output": OUTPUT, "cacheRead": CACHE_READ, "cacheWrite": CACHE_WRITE },
      "claude-opus-5-5": { "input": INPUT, "output": OUTPUT, "cacheRead": CACHE_READ, "cacheWrite": CACHE_WRITE }
    }
  }
}

Replace each placeholder with the provider's current rate in USD per million tokens: DeepSeek, Z.ai, Moonshot, MiniMax, Alibaba Model Studio. Use the model ID without the suffix as the key: deepseek-flash also prices deepseek-flash[1m]. With server-side mapping, key the Claude model ID Claude Code sends (claude-opus-5-5 above) and give it the rates of the provider model it maps to. If the file already exists, add the modelPricing key to it. Reference: Claude Code settings, modelPricing.

agent-otel-kit never writes this file; setup edits only ~/.claude/settings.json.

The collector cannot see that a pricing table is in effect, so tell it: add cost.basis=managed to OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES in the env of ~/.claude/settings.json. Claude Code copies resource attributes onto every metric and event, and the dashboards then count that cost as exact. Set cost.basis=list instead for a gateway in front of Anthropic itself, whose cost is Anthropic list price.

Which provider

anthropic.custom_base_url does not say which provider a session used, and with server-side mapping the model name does not either. Tag it on the agent, for example "OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES": "llm.provider=deepseek,cost.basis=managed"; every Claude Code series then carries an llm_provider label.

Subscription plans

On a flat-rate coding plan (GLM Coding Plan, Kimi membership, MiniMax and Alibaba coding plans) a per-token dollar figure means nothing: you pay for a quota, not per token. Look at the token panels, which are exact, and ignore the cost panels or set the Cost basis selector to list.

Perses

docker compose --profile perses up -d      # or: make up-perses

Perses starts on http://localhost:8080 with the project agent-otel-kit, global datasources for Prometheus, Loki and Tempo, and the three dashboards, all loaded from perses/provisioning/ (re-read every 30 s). The dashboards are plain Perses resources (kind: Dashboard) and can also be applied to another Perses server with percli apply -d perses/provisioning/dashboards/.

Troubleshooting

  • agent-otel-kit doctor prints one line per check: stack health, whether the collector has received anything (from its own otelcol_receiver_accepted_* counters), which agent_name values have metrics in Prometheus, and whether each agent config points at the collector.
  • Loki and Tempo answer 503 for up to a minute after docker compose up.
  • Nothing arrives: telemetry settings are read at agent start, so start a new session after setup. A shell variable such as OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT can point elsewhere; doctor warns about it. Claude Code ignores OTel exporter variables in project-level .claude/settings.json. Qwen Code lets QWEN_TELEMETRY_* variables and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT override ~/.qwen/settings.json.
  • Metrics arrive late: Claude Code exports metrics every 60 s unless OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL is set (setup sets 10 s); events and spans export every 5 s.
  • No traces from Claude Code: the traces beta needs CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1 and OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp.
  • To see raw data, start with make up-debug and run docker compose logs -f otel-collector.
  • make test-collector runs the collector config against payloads recorded from Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code and Claude Code (in collector/testdata/) and checks the normalization, the tool histogram, the redaction, and the Claude Code model suffix and cost basis.
  • Restarting the collector resets its delta-to-cumulative state; the dashboards treat that as a counter reset.
  • Memory limits: collector, Prometheus, Loki and Tempo 512 MiB each, Grafana 384 MiB, Perses 256 MiB.
  • make clean stops the stack and deletes its volumes.

Layout

compose.yaml               the stack (Perses under --profile perses)
collector/config.yaml      receivers, processors, connector, exporters
prometheus/ loki/ tempo/   backend configs
grafana/                   datasources and dashboards
perses/                    Perses config and provisioning
cmd/agent-otel-kit/        CLI: setup, setup --undo, doctor, version
.goreleaser.yaml           release builds (a vX.Y.Z tag runs .github/workflows/release.yml)
tools/gendashboards/       generates the Grafana and Perses dashboards
scripts/                   demo.sh (real claude -p sessions), screenshots.sh,
                           test-collector.sh (collector rules on recorded payloads),
                           check-collector-warnings.sh (collector start-up warnings)

한국어

명령 한 줄(docker compose up)로 Claude Code·Codex·Gemini CLI·Qwen Code의 비용, 토큰, 도구 호출, 트레이스를 내 컴퓨터에서 봅니다.

agent-otel-kit은 AI 코딩 에이전트용 로컬 OpenTelemetry 스택입니다. 에이전트의 OTLP 텔레메트리를 받는 OpenTelemetry Collector, 메트릭용 Prometheus, 이벤트용 Loki, 트레이스용 Tempo, 그리고 Grafana와 Perses에 같은 대시보드 3개가 들어 있습니다. 작은 Go CLI가 각 에이전트 설정을 collector로 향하게 하고 데이터가 들어오는지 확인합니다.

빠른 시작 (30초)

필요한 것: compose 플러그인이 있는 Docker, 그리고 CLI(CLI 설치 참고).

git clone https://github.com/s3onghyun/agent-otel-kit && cd agent-otel-kit
docker compose up -d                       # 또는 make up
brew install s3onghyun/tap/agent-otel-kit  # 또는 릴리스 압축 파일, go install, make build
agent-otel-kit setup claude                # codex, gemini, qwen, all도 가능
# 에이전트 세션을 새로 시작해 1분쯤 쓴 뒤:
agent-otel-kit doctor

Grafana는 http://localhost:3000입니다(익명 읽기 허용, 대시보드는 "Agent OTel Kit" 폴더). Perses는 docker compose --profile perses up -d 후 http://localhost:8080에서 엽니다.

모든 포트는 127.0.0.1에만 열립니다. collector는 localhost:4318(OTLP/HTTP)과 localhost:4317(OTLP/gRPC)에서 받습니다.

CLI 설치

  • Homebrew(macOS, Linux): brew install s3onghyun/tap/agent-otel-kit
  • Linux·macOS(amd64, arm64)용 빌드 파일과 checksums.txt: Releases
  • Go 1.24 이상: go install github.com/s3onghyun/agent-otel-kit/cmd/agent-otel-kit@latest
  • 클론한 저장소에서: make build가 bin/agent-otel-kit을 만듭니다

agent-otel-kit version은 버전, 커밋, 빌드 날짜를 출력합니다.

수집하는 것과 수집하지 않는 것

수집: 텔레메트리를 켠 에이전트가 내보내는 메트릭, 이벤트, 트레이스입니다. 비용(Claude Code만), 유형별 토큰 수, 세션, 활동 시간, 도구 호출(이름, 성공 여부, 소요 시간, 권한 결정), 모델 요청 시간, 프롬프트·모델 요청·도구 호출별 span입니다.

기본으로 수집하지 않는 것:

  • 프롬프트 내용, 모델 응답, 도구 인자, 도구 출력, 파일 경로, 셸 명령, 오류 메시지(파일 경로가 들어갈 수 있는 error.message와 span 예외 메시지 포함). 에이전트도 옵트인(OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS, OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS, Codex log_user_prompt, Gemini·Qwen Code logPrompts)하지 않으면 대부분 가립니다. collector의 transform/redact가 이 속성들을 한 번 더 지우므로, 에이전트 쪽 스위치를 실수로 켜도 내용은 저장되지 않습니다. 남기려면 collector 환경 변수 AGENT_OTEL_KIT_CAPTURE_CONTENT=true를 설정합니다.
  • 프로세스 명령줄(process.command_args). Gemini CLI가 resource 속성으로 보내는데, gemini -p "..."로 실행하면 프롬프트가 들어 있습니다.
  • user.email. Claude Code는 모든 데이터에 계정 이메일을 붙이고, Gemini CLI도 Google 로그인 시 그렇다고 문서에 적혀 있습니다(API 키로는 보내지 않았습니다). collector가 지웁니다. 남기려면 AGENT_OTEL_KIT_KEEP_EMAIL=true입니다.
  • Gemini CLI와 Qwen Code는 기본값으로 프롬프트를 기록하므로 setup gemini와 setup qwen이 logPrompts: false를 씁니다. Qwen Code는 프롬프트 기록을 꺼도 백그라운드 서브에이전트의 최종 답변(result, execution_summary)을 보내는데, collector가 이것도 지웁니다.

남는 식별자: session.id(Codex는 conversation.id), user.account_uuid, organization.id, Codex user.account_id, installation.id, terminal.type, 호스트 이름과 OS. 모든 데이터는 내 컴퓨터에만 있고, 스택이 외부로 보내는 것은 없습니다(Grafana와 Loki 사용 통계 전송은 꺼 두었습니다).

에이전트별 설정

setup은 각 에이전트의 사용자 설정 파일만 고칩니다. 처음 실행할 때 원본을 ~/.agent-otel-kit/backups/에 저장하고, setup --undo <agent>는 원본 바이트와 권한을 그대로 되돌립니다. setup이 새로 만든 파일과 디렉터리는 지웁니다. setup 이후 파일을 손으로 고쳤다면 --force 없이는 되돌리지 않습니다. --dry-run은 쓰지 않고 결과만 출력하고, --endpoint로 다른 collector를 지정합니다(기본 http://localhost:4318).

에이전트 파일 setup이 쓰는 내용
Claude Code ~/.claude/settings.json ($CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR 지원) env: CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1, 메트릭·로그 OTLP exporter, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, http/protobuf, 메트릭 주기 10초, 트레이스 베타(OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp, CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1, --no-traces로 생략)
Codex ~/.codex/config.toml ($CODEX_HOME 지원) [otel] 아래 표시된 블록: exporter, trace_exporter, metrics_exporter를 otlp-http와 /v1/logs, /v1/traces, /v1/metrics URL로, log_user_prompt = false. 다른 [otel] 키와 나머지 파일은 그대로 둡니다
Gemini CLI ~/.gemini/settings.json telemetry: enabled, target: "local", otlpEndpoint, otlpProtocol: "http", logPrompts: false. endpoint를 덮어쓰는 outfile은 지웁니다
Qwen Code ~/.qwen/settings.json telemetry: enabled, target: "local", otlpEndpoint, otlpProtocol, logPrompts: false. endpoint를 덮어쓰는 outfile과 신호별 otlpTracesEndpoint, otlpLogsEndpoint, otlpMetricsEndpoint는 지웁니다. setup이 새로 만드는 파일에는 "$version": 4도 넣어 Qwen Code가 첫 실행 때 파일을 다시 쓰지 않게 합니다. privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled(Qwen Code 자체 사용 통계)는 건드리지 않습니다

주석이 있는 설정 파일은 고치지 않고 오류로 멈춥니다. 이때는 블록을 직접 추가합니다.

Qwen Code는 기본으로 OTLP/gRPC(otlpProtocol: "grpc", otlpEndpoint: "http://localhost:4317")를 씁니다. Qwen Code의 OTLP/HTTP exporter가 빈 요청 본문을 보낸다는 이슈가 열려 있기 때문입니다(QwenLM/qwen-code#14466). 아래 0.27.4 실행에서는 OTLP/HTTP도 동작했습니다. setup은 --endpoint의 포트 4318을 4317로 바꿔 gRPC endpoint를 만듭니다. --endpoint가 다른 포트이면(예: setup all --endpoint https://otel.lan/otlp) setup은 --endpoint URL을 otlpProtocol: "http"로 쓰고 안내 문구를 출력합니다. --protocol http는 항상 OTLP/HTTP를, --protocol grpc는 항상 gRPC를 쓰며 포트가 4318이 아닌 endpoint에서는 실패합니다.

지원 버전:

에이전트 상태
Claude Code 2.1.325 실제 스택에서 확인: 메트릭, 이벤트, 트레이스(트레이스 베타 플래그 사용).
Codex 0.169.0 (codex exec) setup codex로 실제 스택에서 확인: 메트릭, 이벤트, 트레이스. 토큰은 codex.turn.token_usage 히스토그램, 세션은 codex.thread.started, 도구 호출은 codex.tool_result 이벤트에서 옵니다. 비용 메트릭은 없습니다. Codex 메트릭에는 세션 ID가 없어 세션별 표에는 Codex 세션이 나오지 않습니다.
Gemini CLI 0.68.0 (gemini -p, API 키) setup gemini로 실제 스택에서 확인: 메트릭, 이벤트, 트레이스. 도구 호출은 gemini_cli.tool_call 이벤트에서 옵니다. 비용 메트릭은 없습니다.
Qwen Code 0.27.4 (qwen -p, OpenAI 호환 인증) setup qwen(gRPC)과 setup qwen --protocol http로 실제 스택에서 확인: 메트릭, 이벤트, 트레이스, read_file 호출 하나와 거부된 셸 호출 하나. 도구 호출은 qwen-code.tool_call 이벤트에서 옵니다. 비용 메트릭은 없습니다. 모델 서버는 실제 provider가 아니라 dummy 키를 쓰는 로컬 OpenAI 호환 mock이었습니다.

비대화형 모드와 위에 적은 인증 방식만 돌려 봤습니다. 개인 Google 로그인으로는 Google이 이 클라이언트를 거부해서("no longer supported for Gemini Code Assist for individuals") Gemini CLI는 AI Studio API 키로 확인했습니다. Qwen Code는 OpenAI 호환 mock 서버로 돌렸습니다. 실제 Alibaba Cloud Model Studio(DashScope)나 DeepSeek 키로도 텔레메트리 경로는 같지만, 그 경우 provider가 실제로 보고하는 모델 이름, 토큰 수(캐시·reasoning 토큰), 지연 시간까지 확인할 수 있습니다.

delta temporality 함정

Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI는 기본적으로 카운터를 delta temporality로 내보내는데(매번 지난 전송 이후 증가분만 보냄. Qwen Code는 누적 카운터를 보냄), Prometheus는 누적(cumulative) 카운터만 저장하기 때문에 OTLP를 그대로 Prometheus로 보내면 값이 버려지거나 잘못 읽힙니다. collector의 delta_to_cumulative processor가 Prometheus exporter 앞에서 시계열별 누적 합계를 유지하므로 에이전트 기본값을 바꿀 필요가 없습니다.

compose.yaml의 관련 Prometheus 설정 두 가지: created-timestamp-zero-ingestion은 시계열이 시작될 때 0 샘플을 넣어 짧은 세션의 첫 전송도 셉니다. promql-extended-range-selectors는 increase(x[$__range] anchored)를 쓸 수 있게 해서, 대시보드가 increase()의 외삽 없이 정확한 합계를 보여 줍니다.

대시보드

세 대시보드 모두 Grafana(grafana/dashboards/)와 Perses(perses/provisioning/dashboards/)에 있습니다. 둘 다 tools/gendashboards의 패널 목록 하나에서 생성하며(make dashboards), 커밋된 JSON이 다르면 CI가 실패합니다.

Agent cost and tokens: 기간 내 비용, 추정 비용(아래 "서드파티 엔드포인트" 절), 토큰, 세션, 활동 시간; 모델별 구간 비용; 유형별 구간 토큰; 모델별 비용; 에이전트·모델·유형별 토큰; 비용이 큰 세션. Cost basis 선택기로 cost_basis별 비용만 볼 수 있습니다.

Agent tool calls: 호출 수, 실패 수, 성공률, p95 소요 시간; 도구별 구간 호출 수와 p95; 도구별 표; 권한 결정(누가 호출을 허용했는지); Loki의 실패 호출 목록. 도구 메트릭 agent_otel_kit.tool.duration은 collector의 signal_to_metrics connector가 각 에이전트의 도구 결과 이벤트로 만들어서 에이전트마다 같은 형태입니다.

Agent sessions and traces: 세션별 비용과 토큰, Tempo의 interaction 트레이스, 트레이스 워터폴(Trace ID 칸에 ID 입력), 모델 요청 시간, 유형별 이벤트 수, 선택한 세션의 이벤트 흐름.

모든 레이블은 각 에이전트가 설정하는 service.name에서 만든 agent_name(claude-code, codex, gemini-cli, qwen-code)으로 통일합니다. 바꾸려면 에이전트에 OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=agent.name=<이름>을 설정합니다. Claude Code 자체의 agent.name 속성(서브에이전트 이름)과 Codex의 agent_name 속성(에이전트 경로, 메인 에이전트는 /root)은 subagent.name으로 남습니다. Codex의 conversation.id는 session.id로, token_type은 type으로 복사합니다.

토큰 합계(Tokens 통계와 세션별 Tokens 열)에는 서로 겹치지 않는 유형만 더합니다. Codex는 캐시 입력을 input에, reasoning을 output에 포함해 세고, Gemini CLI는 cache를 input에, Qwen Code는 cache를 input에, OpenAI 호환 provider에서는 thought(reasoning)를 output에 포함해 세므로 이 부분(과 Codex의 total)은 다시 더하지 않습니다. Claude Code의 cacheRead, cacheCreation은 input과 별개라서 더합니다. 유형별 분석 패널에는 겹치는 유형을 포함해 모든 유형이 표시됩니다.

대시보드에서 보이는 에이전트별 차이:

  • Codex는 실행은 됐지만 0이 아닌 코드로 끝난 셸 명령도 성공한 도구 호출로 기록합니다. code mode에서는 안쪽 exec_command마다 바깥 exec 도구도 함께 기록합니다.
  • Codex는 짧은 내부 트레이스(auth, fs.read_file 등)를 많이 보내므로, 트레이스 패널에는 Codex의 turn/start만 보입니다. Gemini CLI에는 프롬프트 단위 트레이스가 없고, 모델 호출마다 llm_call, 도구 묶음마다 schedule_tool_calls 트레이스를 보냅니다.
  • Codex는 기본 WebSocket 전송에서는 요청별 모델 소요 시간을 기록하지 않아, 모델 요청 패널에는 HTTP /responses 요청만 나옵니다.
  • Qwen Code는 프롬프트마다 qwen-code.interaction 트레이스를 하나 보냅니다. 백그라운드 서브에이전트(메모리 추출기 등)의 모델 호출은 별도의 qwen-code.llm_request 트레이스로 오며, 트레이스 패널에는 나오지 않습니다.
  • Qwen Code는 ~/.qwen/settings.json에 "telemetry": {"metrics": {"includeSessionId": true}}가 있을 때(또는 QWEN_TELEMETRY_METRICS_INCLUDE_SESSION_ID=true)만 메트릭에 session.id를 붙입니다. 세션마다 새 시계열이 생긴다고 Qwen Code가 경고하므로 setup은 켜지 않고, 켜지 않으면 세션별 표에 Qwen Code 세션이 나오지 않습니다. 이벤트와 span에는 항상 session.id가 있습니다.

Prometheus에 실제로 들어온 메트릭 이름. Claude Code 2.1.325: claude_code_cost_usage_USD_total, claude_code_token_usage_tokens_total, claude_code_session_count_total, claude_code_active_time_seconds_total. Codex 0.169.0(짧은 codex exec 실행에서 메트릭 74종) 중: codex_turn_token_usage_{bucket,count,sum}(레이블 token_type), codex_thread_started_total, codex_tool_call_total, codex_turn_e2e_duration_ms_milliseconds_*. Gemini CLI 0.68.0: gemini_cli_token_usage_total(레이블 type: input, output, thought, cache, tool), gemini_cli_session_count_total, gemini_cli_tool_call_count_total, gemini_cli_api_request_count_total. Qwen Code 0.27.4: qwen_code_token_usage_total(레이블 type: input, output, thought, cache), qwen_code_session_count_total, qwen_code_tool_call_count_total(레이블 function_name, decision, success), qwen_code_api_request_count_total, qwen_code_api_request_latency_milliseconds_*. collector가 만드는 것: agent_otel_kit_tool_duration_milliseconds_{bucket,count,sum}. Claude Code에는 claude_code.lines_of_code.count, claude_code.commit.count, claude_code.pull_request.count, claude_code.code_edit_tool.decision도 있지만 편집, 커밋, PR이 있어야 나타납니다.

Loki에서 본 이벤트 이름: Claude Code tool_result, tool_decision, api_request, user_prompt 등; Codex codex.tool_result, codex.tool_decision, codex.sse_event, codex.api_request, codex.user_prompt 등; Gemini CLI gemini_cli.tool_call, gemini_cli.api_request, gemini_cli.api_response, gemini_cli.file_operation, gemini_cli.user_prompt 등; Qwen Code qwen-code.tool_call, qwen-code.api_request, qwen-code.api_response, qwen-code.file_operation, qwen-code.user_prompt 등.

스크린샷은 작성자 컴퓨터에서 실제 세션을 돌린 이 스택에서 찍었습니다: Claude Code(make demo), codex exec, gemini -p, Qwen Code 0.27.4(qwen -p, dummy 키를 쓰는 로컬 OpenAI 호환 mock 모델 서버 대상), 그다음 make screenshots. 맨 위 데모 GIF는 그런 실행 한 번 동안 같은 대시보드를 headless Chromium으로 녹화한 것으로, 자르기와 배속만 했습니다. 원본은 docs/demo.mp4입니다.

서드파티(Anthropic 호환) 엔드포인트로 Claude Code 쓰기

DeepSeek, Z.ai(GLM), Moonshot(Kimi), MiniMax, Alibaba Model Studio는 ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL로 자기 Anthropic 호환 API에 Claude Code를 붙이는 가이드를 냅니다. 이때도 Claude Code는 평소와 같은 텔레메트리를 보내고, kit은 그대로 받습니다. 대시보드에 보이는 것(Claude Code 2.1.325와 로컬 mock 엔드포인트로 측정, 실제 provider로는 아직 확인하지 않음):

  • 토큰 수는 정확합니다. 엔드포인트가 돌려준 usage 숫자 그대로입니다.
  • 비용은 아닙니다. Claude Code는 비용을 Anthropic 단가로 직접 계산합니다. 모르는 모델 ID(deepseek-chat, glm-4.6)에는 기본 모델 단가를 씁니다(2.1.325 기준 100만 토큰당 input $4, output $20, cache read $0.20). provider가 Claude 모델 ID를 자기 쪽에서 바꿔 주는 경우(Claude Code는 claude-opus-5-5를 보내고 provider는 자기 모델로 처리) 메트릭에는 Claude list 가격의 claude-opus-5-5로 찍힙니다. 실제로 응답한 모델은 api_request 이벤트의 model에만 남고, 그것도 provider가 실제 이름을 돌려줄 때만입니다.
  • 이런 세션의 모든 메트릭, 이벤트, span에는 anthropic.custom_base_url=true(Prometheus 레이블 anthropic_custom_base_url)가 붙습니다. kit은 이 값을 그대로 둡니다.

collector가 하는 일:

  • Claude Code 비용 시계열과 api_request 이벤트에 cost_basis를 붙입니다. anthropic.custom_base_url이 true면 estimated, 아니면 list입니다. 에이전트에 직접 설정한 cost.basis는 그대로 둡니다(아래 참고). 비용 대시보드는 Cost (USD)(list와 managed)와 **Estimated cost (USD)**를 따로 보여 주고, 모든 비용 시계열 이름과 세션 표에 basis를 표시합니다.
  • Claude Code 메트릭, 이벤트, span의 model에서 [1m] 같은 컨텍스트 창 suffix를 뗍니다. provider 가이드는 모델 ID를 deepseek-flash[1m]처럼 쓰는데, Claude Code는 API에는 deepseek-flash로 보내면서 텔레메트리에는 suffix를 남겨 한 모델이 시계열 두 개로 갈라지기 때문입니다. Claude Code 자체의 [1m] 모델 ID도 같은 방식으로 합쳐집니다.

정확한 비용: managed 설정의 modelPricing

Claude Code(v2.1.242 이상)는 modelPricing.overrides 표로 모델 단가를 정하고, OpenTelemetry 비용 메트릭과 이벤트에도 적용합니다. 이 표는 managed 설정에서만 읽으며, root 또는 관리자 권한이 필요합니다.

  • Linux: /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json
  • macOS: /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-settings.json
{
  "modelPricing": {
    "overrides": {
      "deepseek-flash": { "input": INPUT, "output": OUTPUT, "cacheRead": CACHE_READ, "cacheWrite": CACHE_WRITE },
      "claude-opus-5-5": { "input": INPUT, "output": OUTPUT, "cacheRead": CACHE_READ, "cacheWrite": CACHE_WRITE }
    }
  }
}

자리표시자마다 provider의 현재 단가(100만 토큰당 USD)를 넣습니다: DeepSeek, Z.ai, Moonshot, MiniMax, Alibaba Model Studio. 키는 suffix 없는 모델 ID로 씁니다. deepseek-flash는 deepseek-flash[1m]에도 적용됩니다. 서버 측 매핑이면 Claude Code가 보내는 Claude 모델 ID(위의 claude-opus-5-5)를 키로 쓰고, 그 ID가 매핑되는 provider 모델의 단가를 넣습니다. 파일이 이미 있으면 modelPricing 키만 추가합니다. 참고: Claude Code 설정, modelPricing.

agent-otel-kit은 이 파일을 쓰지 않습니다. setup은 ~/.claude/settings.json만 고칩니다.

collector는 단가 표가 적용됐는지 알 수 없으므로 직접 알려 줍니다. ~/.claude/settings.json의 env에 있는 OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES에 cost.basis=managed를 넣으면, Claude Code가 resource 속성을 모든 메트릭과 이벤트에 복사하고 대시보드는 그 비용을 정확한 값으로 셉니다. Anthropic 앞에 둔 게이트웨이처럼 비용이 Anthropic list 가격 그대로인 경우에는 cost.basis=list를 넣습니다.

provider 구분

anthropic.custom_base_url만으로는 어느 provider를 썼는지 알 수 없고, 서버 측 매핑이면 모델 이름으로도 알 수 없습니다. 에이전트에 태그를 붙입니다. 예: "OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES": "llm.provider=deepseek,cost.basis=managed". 그러면 Claude Code의 모든 시계열에 llm_provider 레이블이 붙습니다.

구독 플랜

정액 코딩 플랜(GLM Coding Plan, Kimi 멤버십, MiniMax·Alibaba 코딩 플랜)에서는 토큰당 달러 금액이 의미가 없습니다. 토큰 단위가 아니라 사용량 한도에 돈을 내기 때문입니다. 정확한 토큰 패널을 보고, 비용 패널은 무시하거나 Cost basis 선택기를 list로 둡니다.

Perses

docker compose --profile perses up -d      # 또는 make up-perses

Perses가 http://localhost:8080에서 agent-otel-kit 프로젝트, Prometheus·Loki·Tempo 전역 데이터소스, 대시보드 3개와 함께 뜹니다. 모두 perses/provisioning/에서 읽습니다(30초마다 다시 읽음). 대시보드는 일반 Perses 리소스(kind: Dashboard)라서 percli apply -d perses/provisioning/dashboards/로 다른 Perses 서버에도 올릴 수 있습니다.

문제 해결

  • agent-otel-kit doctor는 검사마다 한 줄씩 출력합니다: 스택 상태, collector가 받은 데이터가 있는지(collector 자체의 otelcol_receiver_accepted_* 카운터), Prometheus에 메트릭이 있는 agent_name 값, 각 에이전트 설정이 collector를 가리키는지.
  • Loki와 Tempo는 docker compose up 후 최대 1분 동안 503을 반환합니다.
  • 데이터가 안 들어올 때: 텔레메트리 설정은 에이전트 시작 시 읽으므로 setup 후 세션을 새로 시작합니다. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT 같은 셸 변수가 다른 곳을 가리킬 수 있고, doctor가 경고합니다. Claude Code는 프로젝트의 .claude/settings.json에 있는 OTel exporter 변수를 무시합니다. Qwen Code에서는 QWEN_TELEMETRY_* 변수와 OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT가 ~/.qwen/settings.json보다 우선합니다.
  • 메트릭이 늦게 들어올 때: Claude Code는 OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL이 없으면 60초마다 메트릭을 보냅니다(setup은 10초로 설정). 이벤트와 span은 5초마다 보냅니다.
  • Claude Code 트레이스가 없을 때: 트레이스 베타는 CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1과 OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp가 필요합니다.
  • 원본 데이터를 보려면 make up-debug로 띄우고 docker compose logs -f otel-collector를 봅니다.
  • make test-collector는 Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Claude Code에서 기록한 payload(collector/testdata/)로 collector 설정을 돌려 정규화, 도구 히스토그램, 가림 처리, Claude Code 모델 suffix와 cost basis를 확인합니다.
  • collector를 재시작하면 delta→cumulative 상태가 초기화되고, 대시보드는 이를 카운터 리셋으로 처리합니다.
  • 메모리 상한: collector, Prometheus, Loki, Tempo 각 512 MiB, Grafana 384 MiB, Perses 256 MiB.
  • make clean은 스택을 멈추고 볼륨을 지웁니다.

개발

pull request 전에 돌릴 검사와 collector 설정 변경 체크리스트는 CONTRIBUTING.md에 있습니다.

content_text: See the cost, tokens, tool calls and traces of Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Qwen Code on your own machine, with one docker compose up. 한국어 · 简体中文 agent-otel-kit is a local OpenTelemetry stack for AI coding agents: an OpenTelemetry Collector that receives the agents' OTLP telemetry, Prometheus for metrics, Loki for events, Tempo for traces, and the same three dashboards in Grafana and in Perses. A small Go CLI points each agent at the collector and checks that data arrives. Quickstart (30 seconds) Requirements: Docker with the compose plugin, and the CLI (see Install the CLI). git clone https://github.com/s3onghyun/agent-otel-kit && cd agent-otel-kit docker compose up -d # or: make up brew install s3onghyun/tap/agent-otel-kit # or a release archive, go install, or make build agent-otel-kit setup claude # or codex, gemini, qwen, all # start a new agent session and use it for a minute, then: agent-otel-kit doctor Open Grafana at http://localhost:3000 (anonymous read access; the dashboards are in the "Agent OTel Kit" folder). For Perses, run docker compose --profile perses up -d and open http://localhost:8080. Every port is bound to 127.0.0.1. The collector listens on localhost:4318 (OTLP/HTTP) and localhost:4317 (OTLP/gRPC). Install the CLI Homebrew (macOS, Linux): brew install s3onghyun/tap/agent-otel-kit Prebuilt archives for Linux and macOS (amd64, arm64) with checksums.txt: Releases Go 1.24+: go install github.com/s3onghyun/agent-otel-kit/cmd/agent-otel-kit@latest From the clone: make build writes bin/agent-otel-kit agent-otel-kit version prints the version, commit and build date. What is collected and what is not Collected: the metrics, events and traces each agent exports when telemetry is on: cost (Claude Code only), token counts by type, sessions, active time, tool calls with name, success, duration and permission decision, model request duration, and trace spans for each prompt, model request and tool call. Not collected by default: Prompt text, model responses, tool arguments, tool output, file paths, shell commands and error messages (including error.message and span exception messages, which can hold file paths). The agents already redact most of these unless you opt in (OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS, OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS, Codex log_user_prompt, Gemini and Qwen Code logPrompts). The collector deletes these attributes again in transform/redact, so turning one of those agent switches on by mistake does not store content. Set AGENT_OTEL_KIT_CAPTURE_CONTENT=true in the collector's environment to keep them. The process command line (process.command_args). Gemini CLI sends it as a resource attribute, and for gemini -p "..." it contains the prompt. user.email. Claude Code attaches the account email to every data point, and Gemini CLI documents the same for Google sign-in (with an API key it sent none); the collector drops it unless AGENT_OTEL_KIT_KEEP_EMAIL=true. setup gemini and setup qwen set logPrompts: false, because Gemini CLI and Qwen Code log prompts by default. Qwen Code also sends the final answer of its background subagents (result, execution_summary) with prompt logging off; the collector deletes those too. Other identifiers stay: session.id (Codex: conversation.id), user.account_uuid, organization.id, Codex user.account_id, installation.id, terminal.type, host name and OS. Everything stays on your machine; nothing in the stack sends data elsewhere (Grafana and Loki usage reporting is off). Per-agent setup setup edits only the agent's own user config file. The first run saves the original file under ~/.agent-otel-kit/backups/; setup --undo <agent> puts back the exact original bytes and permissions, or deletes the file (and any directory) that setup created. If you edited the file after setup, undo refuses unless you pass --force. --dry-run prints the result without writing. --endpoint points agents at a collector elsewhere (default http://localhost:4318). Agent File What setup writes Claude Code ~/.claude/settings.json ($CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR honoured) env: CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1, OTLP exporters for metrics and logs, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, http/protobuf, a 10 s metric interval, and the traces beta (OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp, CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1; skip with --no-traces) Codex ~/.codex/config.toml ($CODEX_HOME honoured) a marked block under [otel]: exporter, trace_exporter and metrics_exporter as otlp-http with the /v1/logs, /v1/traces, /v1/metrics URLs, log_user_prompt = false; other [otel] keys and the rest of the file are kept Gemini CLI ~/.gemini/settings.json telemetry: enabled, target: "local", otlpEndpoint, otlpProtocol: "http", logPrompts: false; removes outfile, which would override the endpoint Qwen Code ~/.qwen/settings.json telemetry: enabled, target: "local", otlpEndpoint, otlpProtocol, logPrompts: false; removes outfile and the per-signal otlpTracesEndpoint, otlpLogsEndpoint, otlpMetricsEndpoint, which would override the endpoint. A file setup creates also gets "$version": 4, so Qwen Code does not rewrite it on first start. privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled (Qwen Code's own usage statistics) is left as it is Settings files with comments are not edited (setup stops with an error); add the block by hand in that case. Qwen Code uses OTLP/gRPC by default (otlpProtocol: "grpc", otlpEndpoint: "http://localhost:4317"), because its OTLP/HTTP exporter has an open report of sending empty request bodies (QwenLM/qwen-code#14466); OTLP/HTTP worked in the 0.27.4 runs below. setup takes the gRPC endpoint from --endpoint by replacing port 4318 with 4317. When --endpoint is on another port (for example setup all --endpoint https://otel.lan/otlp), setup writes the --endpoint URL with otlpProtocol: "http" instead and prints a notice. --protocol http always writes OTLP/HTTP; --protocol grpc always writes gRPC and fails for an endpoint not on port 4318. Supported versions: Agent Status Claude Code 2.1.325 Verified on a live stack: metrics, events and traces (with the traces beta flag). Codex 0.169.0 (codex exec) Verified on a live stack with setup codex: metrics, events and traces. Tokens come from the codex.turn.token_usage histogram, sessions from codex.thread.started, tool calls from codex.tool_result events. No cost metric. Codex metrics carry no session ID, so Codex sessions are missing from the per-session table. Gemini CLI 0.68.0 (gemini -p, API key) Verified on a live stack with setup gemini: metrics, events and traces. Tool calls come from gemini_cli.tool_call events. No cost metric. Qwen Code 0.27.4 (qwen -p, OpenAI-compatible auth) Verified on a live stack with setup qwen (gRPC) and setup qwen --protocol http: metrics, events and traces, with a read_file call and a denied shell call. Tool calls come from qwen-code.tool_call events. No cost metric. The model server was a local OpenAI-compatible mock with a dummy key, not a real provider. Only the non-interactive modes and the auth methods listed were run. Gemini CLI with a personal Google login was rejected by Google for this client ("no longer supported for Gemini Code Assist for individuals"), so that path was tested with an AI Studio API key. Qwen Code was run against a mock OpenAI-compatible server: the telemetry path is the same with a real Alibaba Cloud Model Studio (DashScope) or DeepSeek key, but such a run would additionally show the model names, token counts (cache and reasoning tokens) and latencies those providers really report. The delta temporality trap Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI export counters with delta temporality by default (each export carries only the increase since the last one; Qwen Code sends cumulative counters), and Prometheus only stores cumulative counters, so a plain OTLP-to-Prometheus path drops or misreads them. The collector's delta_to_cumulative processor keeps a running total per series before the Prometheus exporter, so the agents can keep their defaults. Two related Prometheus settings in compose.yaml: created-timestamp-zero-ingestion inserts a zero sample when a series starts, so a short session's first export is counted, and promql-extended-range-selectors enables increase(x[$__range] anchored), which the dashboards use for exact totals without increase()'s extrapolation. Dashboards All three exist in Grafana (grafana/dashboards/) and Perses (perses/provisioning/dashboards/). Both are generated from one panel list in tools/gendashboards (make dashboards); CI fails if the committed JSON differs. Agent cost and tokens: cost, estimated cost (see third-party endpoints), tokens, sessions and active time for the range; cost per interval by model; tokens per interval by type; cost by model; tokens by agent, model and type; the most expensive sessions. The Cost basis selector filters cost by cost_basis. Agent tool calls: call count, failures, success rate and p95 duration; calls per interval and p95 duration by tool; a per-tool table; permission decisions (who allowed each call); failed calls from Loki. The tool metric agent_otel_kit.tool.duration is built in the collector by the signal_to_metrics connector from each agent's tool result events, so it is the same for all agents. Agent sessions and traces: per-session cost and tokens, the interaction traces from Tempo, a trace waterfall (paste a trace ID into the Trace ID box), model request duration, event rate by type, and the event stream of the selected sessions. Every label is normalized to agent_name (claude-code, codex, gemini-cli, qwen-code), derived from the service.name each agent sets. Set OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=agent.name=<name> on an agent to override it. Claude Code's own agent.name attribute (the subagent name) and Codex's agent_name attribute (the agent path, /root for the main agent) are kept as subagent.name. Codex's conversation.id is copied to session.id, and its token_type to type. Token totals (the Tokens stat and the per-session Tokens column) add only token types that do not overlap: Codex counts cached input inside input and reasoning inside output, Gemini CLI counts cache inside input, and Qwen Code counts cache inside input and, with OpenAI-compatible providers, thought (reasoning) inside output, so those parts (and Codex's total) are not added again. Claude Code's cacheRead and cacheCreation are separate from input and are added. The per-type breakdowns show every type, including the overlapping ones. Agent differences visible on the dashboards: Codex marks a shell command that ran but exited non-zero as a successful tool call. In code mode it also reports the outer exec tool next to each inner exec_command. Codex sends many short internal traces (auth, fs.read_file, ...); the traces panel lists only turn/start for Codex. Gemini CLI has no per-prompt trace: it sends one llm_call trace per model call and one schedule_tool_calls trace per tool batch. Over its default WebSocket transport, Codex logs no per-request model duration, so the model request panel shows Codex only for HTTP /responses requests. Qwen Code sends one qwen-code.interaction trace per prompt. Model calls of its background subagents (such as the memory extractor) arrive as separate qwen-code.llm_request traces, which the traces panel does not list. Qwen Code adds session.id to metrics only with "telemetry": {"metrics": {"includeSessionId": true}} in ~/.qwen/settings.json (or QWEN_TELEMETRY_METRICS_INCLUDE_SESSION_ID=true). setup leaves it off, because Qwen Code warns that it creates new time series for every session, so without it Qwen Code sessions are missing from the per-session table. Events and spans always carry session.id. Metric names seen in Prometheus from Claude Code 2.1.325: claude_code_cost_usage_USD_total, claude_code_token_usage_tokens_total, claude_code_session_count_total, claude_code_active_time_seconds_total. From Codex 0.169.0 (74 metric families in a short codex exec run), among them: codex_turn_token_usage_{bucket,count,sum} (label token_type), codex_thread_started_total, codex_tool_call_total, codex_turn_e2e_duration_ms_milliseconds_*. From Gemini CLI 0.68.0: gemini_cli_token_usage_total (label type: input, output, thought, cache, tool), gemini_cli_session_count_total, gemini_cli_tool_call_count_total, gemini_cli_api_request_count_total. From Qwen Code 0.27.4: qwen_code_token_usage_total (label type: input, output, thought, cache), qwen_code_session_count_total, qwen_code_tool_call_count_total (labels function_name, decision, success), qwen_code_api_request_count_total, qwen_code_api_request_latency_milliseconds_*. From the collector: agent_otel_kit_tool_duration_milliseconds_{bucket,count,sum}. Event names seen in Loki: Claude Code tool_result, tool_decision, api_request, user_prompt, ...; Codex codex.tool_result, codex.tool_decision, codex.sse_event, codex.api_request, codex.user_prompt, ...; Gemini CLI gemini_cli.tool_call, gemini_cli.api_request, gemini_cli.api_response, gemini_cli.file_operation, gemini_cli.user_prompt, ...; Qwen Code qwen-code.tool_call, qwen-code.api_request, qwen-code.api_response, qwen-code.file_operation, qwen-code.user_prompt, .... Claude Code also defines claude_code.lines_of_code.count, claude_code.commit.count, claude_code.pull_request.count and claude_code.code_edit_tool.decision, which only appear after edits, commits or pull requests. The screenshots were taken from this stack with real sessions run on the author's machine: Claude Code (make demo), codex exec, gemini -p and Qwen Code 0.27.4 (qwen -p, against a local OpenAI-compatible mock model server with a dummy key), then make screenshots. The demo GIF at the top is a headless Chromium recording of the same dashboards during one such run, only trimmed and sped up; docs/demo.mp4 is its source. Claude Code with third-party (Anthropic-compatible) endpoints DeepSeek, Z.ai (GLM), Moonshot (Kimi), MiniMax and Alibaba Model Studio publish guides for running Claude Code against their Anthropic-compatible APIs through ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. Claude Code then exports the same telemetry as usual, and the kit receives it without changes. What the dashboards show, measured with Claude Code 2.1.325 against a local mock of such an endpoint (not yet against the providers themselves): Token counts are exact: they are the usage numbers the endpoint returns. Cost is not. Claude Code computes cost locally at Anthropic rates. A model ID it does not know (deepseek-chat, glm-4.6) is priced at the rate of its default model ($4 input, $20 output, $0.20 cache read per million tokens in 2.1.325). When the provider maps Claude model IDs on its side (Claude Code sends claude-opus-5-5, the provider runs its own model), the metrics say claude-opus-5-5 at Claude list price. The model that answered appears only in the api_request event's model, and only if the provider returns its real name. Every metric, event and span of such a session carries anthropic.custom_base_url=true (Prometheus label anthropic_custom_base_url). The kit keeps it. What the collector does with it: It labels each Claude Code cost series and api_request event with cost_basis: estimated when anthropic.custom_base_url is true, otherwise list. A cost.basis you set on the agent yourself is kept (see below). The cost dashboard shows Cost (USD) (list and managed) and Estimated cost (USD) as separate numbers, and names the basis in every cost series and in the session tables. It strips a context-window suffix such as [1m] from model on Claude Code metrics, events and spans. The provider guides write model IDs as deepseek-flash[1m]; Claude Code sends deepseek-flash to the API but keeps the suffix in its telemetry, which would split one model into two series. Claude Code's own [1m] model IDs are merged the same way. Exact cost: modelPricing in managed settings Claude Code (v2.1.242 or later) prices models from a modelPricing.overrides table, and applies it to the OpenTelemetry cost metric and events too. It reads the table only from managed settings, which need root or administrator rights: Linux: /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json macOS: /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-settings.json { "modelPricing": { "overrides": { "deepseek-flash": { "input": INPUT, "output": OUTPUT, "cacheRead": CACHE_READ, "cacheWrite": CACHE_WRITE }, "claude-opus-5-5": { "input": INPUT, "output": OUTPUT, "cacheRead": CACHE_READ, "cacheWrite": CACHE_WRITE } } } } Replace each placeholder with the provider's current rate in USD per million tokens: DeepSeek, Z.ai, Moonshot, MiniMax, Alibaba Model Studio. Use the model ID without the suffix as the key: deepseek-flash also prices deepseek-flash[1m]. With server-side mapping, key the Claude model ID Claude Code sends (claude-opus-5-5 above) and give it the rates of the provider model it maps to. If the file already exists, add the modelPricing key to it. Reference: Claude Code settings, modelPricing. agent-otel-kit never writes this file; setup edits only ~/.claude/settings.json. The collector cannot see that a pricing table is in effect, so tell it: add cost.basis=managed to OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES in the env of ~/.claude/settings.json. Claude Code copies resource attributes onto every metric and event, and the dashboards then count that cost as exact. Set cost.basis=list instead for a gateway in front of Anthropic itself, whose cost is Anthropic list price. Which provider anthropic.custom_base_url does not say which provider a session used, and with server-side mapping the model name does not either. Tag it on the agent, for example "OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES": "llm.provider=deepseek,cost.basis=managed"; every Claude Code series then carries an llm_provider label. Subscription plans On a flat-rate coding plan (GLM Coding Plan, Kimi membership, MiniMax and Alibaba coding plans) a per-token dollar figure means nothing: you pay for a quota, not per token. Look at the token panels, which are exact, and ignore the cost panels or set the Cost basis selector to list. Perses docker compose --profile perses up -d # or: make up-perses Perses starts on http://localhost:8080 with the project agent-otel-kit, global datasources for Prometheus, Loki and Tempo, and the three dashboards, all loaded from perses/provisioning/ (re-read every 30 s). The dashboards are plain Perses resources (kind: Dashboard) and can also be applied to another Perses server with percli apply -d perses/provisioning/dashboards/. Troubleshooting agent-otel-kit doctor prints one line per check: stack health, whether the collector has received anything (from its own otelcol_receiver_accepted_* counters), which agent_name values have metrics in Prometheus, and whether each agent config points at the collector. Loki and Tempo answer 503 for up to a minute after docker compose up. Nothing arrives: telemetry settings are read at agent start, so start a new session after setup. A shell variable such as OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT can point elsewhere; doctor warns about it. Claude Code ignores OTel exporter variables in project-level .claude/settings.json. Qwen Code lets QWEN_TELEMETRY_* variables and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT override ~/.qwen/settings.json. Metrics arrive late: Claude Code exports metrics every 60 s unless OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL is set (setup sets 10 s); events and spans export every 5 s. No traces from Claude Code: the traces beta needs CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1 and OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp. To see raw data, start with make up-debug and run docker compose logs -f otel-collector. make test-collector runs the collector config against payloads recorded from Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code and Claude Code (in collector/testdata/) and checks the normalization, the tool histogram, the redaction, and the Claude Code model suffix and cost basis. Restarting the collector resets its delta-to-cumulative state; the dashboards treat that as a counter reset. Memory limits: collector, Prometheus, Loki and Tempo 512 MiB each, Grafana 384 MiB, Perses 256 MiB. make clean stops the stack and deletes its volumes. Layout compose.yaml the stack (Perses under --profile perses) collector/config.yaml receivers, processors, connector, exporters prometheus/ loki/ tempo/ backend configs grafana/ datasources and dashboards perses/ Perses config and provisioning cmd/agent-otel-kit/ CLI: setup, setup --undo, doctor, version .goreleaser.yaml release builds (a vX.Y.Z tag runs .github/workflows/release.yml) tools/gendashboards/ generates the Grafana and Perses dashboards scripts/ demo.sh (real claude -p sessions), screenshots.sh, test-collector.sh (collector rules on recorded payloads), check-collector-warnings.sh (collector start-up warnings) Development Checks to run before a pull request, and a checklist for collector config changes: CONTRIBUTING.md. Claude Code는 비용을 Anthropic 단가로 직접 계산합니다. 모르는 모델 ID(deepseek-chat, glm-4.6)에는 기본 모델 단가를 씁니다(2.1.325 기준 100만 토큰당 input $4, output $20, cache read $0.20). provider가 Claude 모델 ID를 자기 쪽에서 바꿔 주는 경우(Claude Code는 claude-opus-5-5를 보내고 provider는 자기 모델로 처리) 메트릭에는 Claude list 가격의 claude-opus-5-5로 찍힙니다. 실제로 응답한 모델은 api_request 이벤트의 model에만 남고, 그것도 provider가 실제 이름을 돌려줄 때만입니다. 이런 세션의 모든 메트릭, 이벤트, span에는 anthropic.custom_base_url=true(Prometheus 레이블 anthropic_custom_base_url)가 붙습니다. kit은 이 값을 그대로 둡니다. collector가 하는 일: Claude Code 비용 시계열과 api_request 이벤트에 cost_basis를 붙입니다. anthropic.custom_base_url이 true면 estimated, 아니면 list입니다. 에이전트에 직접 설정한 cost.basis는 그대로 둡니다(아래 참고). 비용 대시보드는 Cost (USD)(list와 managed)와 **Estimated cost (USD)**를 따로 보여 주고, 모든 비용 시계열 이름과 세션 표에 basis를 표시합니다. Claude Code 메트릭, 이벤트, span의 model에서 [1m] 같은 컨텍스트 창 suffix를 뗍니다. provider 가이드는 모델 ID를 deepseek-flash[1m]처럼 쓰는데, Claude Code는 API에는 deepseek-flash로 보내면서 텔레메트리에는 suffix를 남겨 한 모델이 시계열 두 개로 갈라지기 때문입니다. Claude Code 자체의 [1m] 모델 ID도 같은 방식으로 합쳐집니다. 정확한 비용: managed 설정의 modelPricing Claude Code(v2.1.242 이상)는 modelPricing.overrides 표로 모델 단가를 정하고, OpenTelemetry 비용 메트릭과 이벤트에도 적용합니다. 이 표는 managed 설정에서만 읽으며, root 또는 관리자 권한이 필요합니다. Linux: /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json macOS: /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-settings.json { "modelPricing": { "overrides": { "deepseek-flash": { "input": INPUT, "output": OUTPUT, "cacheRead": CACHE_READ, "cacheWrite": CACHE_WRITE }, "claude-opus-5-5": { "input": INPUT, "output": OUTPUT, "cacheRead": CACHE_READ, "cacheWrite": CACHE_WRITE } } } } 자리표시자마다 provider의 현재 단가(100만 토큰당 USD)를 넣습니다: DeepSeek, Z.ai, Moonshot, MiniMax, Alibaba Model Studio. 키는 suffix 없는 모델 ID로 씁니다. deepseek-flash는 deepseek-flash[1m]에도 적용됩니다. 서버 측 매핑이면 Claude Code가 보내는 Claude 모델 ID(위의 claude-opus-5-5)를 키로 쓰고, 그 ID가 매핑되는 provider 모델의 단가를 넣습니다. 파일이 이미 있으면 modelPricing 키만 추가합니다. 참고: Claude Code 설정, modelPricing. agent-otel-kit은 이 파일을 쓰지 않습니다. setup은 ~/.claude/settings.json만 고칩니다. collector는 단가 표가 적용됐는지 알 수 없으므로 직접 알려 줍니다. ~/.claude/settings.json의 env에 있는 OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES에 cost.basis=managed를 넣으면, Claude Code가 resource 속성을 모든 메트릭과 이벤트에 복사하고 대시보드는 그 비용을 정확한 값으로 셉니다. Anthropic 앞에 둔 게이트웨이처럼 비용이 Anthropic list 가격 그대로인 경우에는 cost.basis=list를 넣습니다. provider 구분 anthropic.custom_base_url만으로는 어느 provider를 썼는지 알 수 없고, 서버 측 매핑이면 모델 이름으로도 알 수 없습니다. 에이전트에 태그를 붙입니다. 예: "OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES": "llm.provider=deepseek,cost.basis=managed". 그러면 Claude Code의 모든 시계열에 llm_provider 레이블이 붙습니다. 구독 플랜 정액 코딩 플랜(GLM Coding Plan, Kimi 멤버십, MiniMax·Alibaba 코딩 플랜)에서는 토큰당 달러 금액이 의미가 없습니다. 토큰 단위가 아니라 사용량 한도에 돈을 내기 때문입니다. 정확한 토큰 패널을 보고, 비용 패널은 무시하거나 Cost basis 선택기를 list로 둡니다. Perses docker compose --profile perses up -d # 또는 make up-perses Perses가 http://localhost:8080에서 agent-otel-kit 프로젝트, Prometheus·Loki·Tempo 전역 데이터소스, 대시보드 3개와 함께 뜹니다. 모두 perses/provisioning/에서 읽습니다(30초마다 다시 읽음). 대시보드는 일반 Perses 리소스(kind: Dashboard)라서 percli apply -d perses/provisioning/dashboards/로 다른 Perses 서버에도 올릴 수 있습니다. 문제 해결 agent-otel-kit doctor는 검사마다 한 줄씩 출력합니다: 스택 상태, collector가 받은 데이터가 있는지(collector 자체의 otelcol_receiver_accepted_* 카운터), Prometheus에 메트릭이 있는 agent_name 값, 각 에이전트 설정이 collector를 가리키는지. Loki와 Tempo는 docker compose up 후 최대 1분 동안 503을 반환합니다. 데이터가 안 들어올 때: 텔레메트리 설정은 에이전트 시작 시 읽으므로 setup 후 세션을 새로 시작합니다. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT 같은 셸 변수가 다른 곳을 가리킬 수 있고, doctor가 경고합니다. Claude Code는 프로젝트의 .claude/settings.json에 있는 OTel exporter 변수를 무시합니다. Qwen Code에서는 QWEN_TELEMETRY_* 변수와 OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT가 ~/.qwen/settings.json보다 우선합니다. 메트릭이 늦게 들어올 때: Claude Code는 OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL이 없으면 60초마다 메트릭을 보냅니다(setup은 10초로 설정). 이벤트와 span은 5초마다 보냅니다. Claude Code 트레이스가 없을 때: 트레이스 베타는 CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1과 OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp가 필요합니다. 원본 데이터를 보려면 make up-debug로 띄우고 docker compose logs -f otel-collector를 봅니다. make test-collector는 Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Claude Code에서 기록한 payload(collector/testdata/)로 collector 설정을 돌려 정규화, 도구 히스토그램, 가림 처리, Claude Code 모델 suffix와 cost basis를 확인합니다. collector를 재시작하면 delta→cumulative 상태가 초기화되고, 대시보드는 이를 카운터 리셋으로 처리합니다. 메모리 상한: collector, Prometheus, Loki, Tempo 각 512 MiB, Grafana 384 MiB, Perses 256 MiB. make clean은 스택을 멈추고 볼륨을 지웁니다. 개발 pull request 전에 돌릴 검사와 collector 설정 변경 체크리스트는 CONTRIBUTING.md에 있습니다. 라이선스: Apache-2.0.
